context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides public and academic libraries with catalogue management, circulation control, and self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and meets high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Students, Public Citizens)
* Circulation Staff and Library Administrators
* Library Management System (Internal Software System)
* Identity Provider / SSO (External System supporting SAML/Shibboleth and local accounts)
* Digital Content Providers (External Vendor Systems for e-books/audiobooks)
* Notification Gateway (External SMS/Email Provider)
* Observability & Logging Platform (Prometheus/Grafana)

## Relationships
* Patrons, Staff, and Administrators to Library Management System via HTTPS (Web/Mobile) using TLS 1.3
* Library Management System to Identity Provider via OIDC/SAML over HTTPS
* Library Management System to Digital Content Providers via HTTPS/REST with mutual TLS (mTLS)
* Library Management System to Notification Gateway via asynchronous HTTPS/REST webhooks

## Technology Stack
* OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with JWT: Secure, token-based authentication and authorization
* TLS 1.3 and mTLS: Mandatory encryption for all internal and external network communications
* Asynchronous Message Queues: Decouples notification dispatch and third-party integrations to protect performance
* EU-pinned Cloud Regions: Ensures strict compliance with EU-only data residency and GDPR constraints

## Rationale
This architecture offloads federated authentication and third-party digital lending while strictly isolating PII within EU boundaries. Asynchronous processing and caching layers guarantee the 99th-percentile search response time remains below 800 ms.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- Solution: Library Management System providing catalogue management, circulation control, and self-service portals.
- Purpose: Deliver high-performance search (<800ms) and secure operations for public and academic libraries while enforcing strict EU-only data residency.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons [person]
- Circulation Staff and Library Administrators [person]
- Identity Provider / SSO [externalSystem]
- Digital Content Providers [externalSystem]
- Notification Gateway [externalSystem]
- Observability & Logging Platform [externalSystem]
- Web Portal [container, React/TypeScript on Nginx]
- API Gateway [container, Envoy/Kong]
- Core Services API [container, Java/Spring Boot]
- Search & Catalogue Service [container, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch]
- Database [container, PostgreSQL with EU hosting]

## Relationships
- Library Patrons -> Web Portal (HTTPS/TLS 1.3)
- Circulation Staff and Library Administrators -> Web Portal (HTTPS/TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider / SSO (OIDC/SAML over HTTPS)
- Web Portal -> API Gateway (HTTPS / JSON over TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway -> Core Services API (gRPC over mTLS)
- API Gateway -> Search & Catalogue Service (gRPC over mTLS)
- Core Services API -> Database (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3)
- Search & Catalogue Service -> Database (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3)
- Core Services API -> Notification Gateway (Asynchronous HTTPS/REST webhooks over TLS 1.3)
- Core Services API -> Digital Content Providers (HTTPS/REST with mutual TLS)

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React/TypeScript on Nginx for the Web Portal
- Routing & Edge: Envoy/Kong API Gateway with circuit breaking and OIDC validation
- Backend Logic: Java/Spring Boot for Core Services API
- Search Engine: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for sub-800ms catalogue queries
- Primary Data Store: PostgreSQL with EU hosting and encrypted persistent volumes
- Infrastructure: Kubernetes with EU-hosted worker nodes, Istio/Linkerd service mesh, and Vault for secrets

## Rationale
- Separates patron-facing search workloads from core transactional operations to easily satisfy the sub-800ms performance SLA (R-05).
- Enforces EU-only data residency via dedicated regional deployments and encrypted storage to maintain compliance and security.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides public and academic libraries with catalogue management, circulation control, and self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons [person]
- Circulation Staff and Library Administrators [person]
- Web Portal [container, React/TypeScript on Nginx]
- API Gateway [container, Envoy/Kong]
- Core Services API [container, Java/Spring Boot]
- Search & Catalogue Service [container, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch]
- Database [container, PostgreSQL with EU hosting]
- Identity Provider / SSO [externalSystem]
- Digital Content Providers [externalSystem]
- Notification Gateway [externalSystem]
- Observability & Logging Platform [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Web Portal -> API Gateway [HTTPS / JSON over TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway -> Core Services API [gRPC over mTLS with W3C Trace Context]
- API Gateway -> Search & Catalogue Service [gRPC over mTLS with W3C Trace Context]
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider / SSO [OIDC/SAML over HTTPS]
- Core Services API -> Database [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Search & Catalogue Service -> Database [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Core Services API -> Notification Gateway [Asynchronous HTTPS/REST webhooks over TLS 1.3]
- Core Services API -> Digital Content Providers [HTTPS/REST with mutual TLS]

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript on Nginx: Powers responsive web interfaces for patrons and staff.
- Envoy/Kong: Provides high-performance edge routing, rate limiting, and security termination.
- Java/Spring Boot: Executes core business logic and transactional processing reliably.
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch: Delivers sub-800ms catalogue search performance.
- PostgreSQL: Ensures reliable relational data storage with strict EU-only residency compliance.
- Redis: Backs distributed rate-limiting to prevent automated scraping.

## Rationale
This microservices-based architecture uses Envoy/Kong for edge protection and decoupled Java/Spring Boot and Elasticsearch services to guarantee sub-800ms performance. Strict TLS 1.3, mTLS, and EU-hosted PostgreSQL ensure regulatory compliance and data security.

Core Services API.analysis:
## Overview
The Core Services API is a Java/Spring Boot container that orchestrates library transactions, circulation management, and integration with external digital providers. It provides secure, low-latency business logic for patrons and staff while enforcing strict EU-only data residency requirements.

## Key Elements
- Core Services API (Java/Spring Boot container)
- Circulation Management Component
- Patron Account Component
- Integration Orchestrator Component
- Database (PostgreSQL with EU hosting)
- API Gateway (Envoy/Kong)
- Notification Gateway
- Digital Content Providers
- Observability & Logging Platform (Prometheus/Grafana)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Core Services API: Routes core requests [gRPC over mTLS with OAuth2 metadata headers]
- Circulation Management Component -> Database: Persists loans and audit events [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Patron Account Component -> Database: Validates memberships [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Integration Orchestrator Component -> Notification Gateway: Dispatches alerts [Asynchronous HTTPS/REST webhooks over TLS 1.3]
- Integration Orchestrator Component -> Digital Content Providers: Brokers external licensing [HTTPS/REST with mutual TLS]
- Core Services API -> Observability & Logging Platform: Emits sanitized distributed traces [OpenTelemetry over gRPC / TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- Java/Spring Boot: Provides a robust framework for modular monolith decomposition and enterprise business logic.
- PostgreSQL with EU Hosting: Ensures persistent relational storage compliant with EU-only data residency mandates.
- gRPC over mTLS: Delivers high-performance, secure internal communication between the API Gateway and Core Services API.
- Resilience4j: Implements circuit breaking to isolate volatile external digital content vendors.
- OpenTelemetry: Captures distributed tracing to satisfy performance SLAs under load.

## Rationale
This modular architecture isolates volatile external dependencies to prevent thread pool exhaustion while maintaining strict transactional integrity. It guarantees high performance, secure token propagation, and strict adherence to EU data residency mandates.

Search & Catalogue Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides public and academic libraries with catalogue management, circulation control, and self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons [person]
- Circulation Staff and Library Administrators [person]
- Web Portal (React/TypeScript on Nginx) [container]
- API Gateway (Envoy/Kong) [container]
- Core Services API (Java/Spring Boot) [container]
- Search & Catalogue Service (OpenSearch/Java) [container]
  - Search API Handler (Java/Spring Boot) [component]
  - Query Builder & Faceting Engine (Java) [component]
  - Indexing Worker (Java/Spring Boot) [component]
  - Search Engine Index (OpenSearch) [component]
- Database (PostgreSQL with EU hosting) [container]
- Identity Provider / SSO [externalSystem]
- Notification Gateway [externalSystem]
- Observability & Logging Platform (Prometheus/Grafana) [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Library Patrons -> Web Portal [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Web Portal -> API Gateway [HTTPS / JSON over TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway -> Search & Catalogue Service [gRPC over mTLS]
- Search & Catalogue Service -> Database [PostgreSQL Replication Protocol over TLS 1.3 via Debezium CDC]
- Search API Handler -> Query Builder & Faceting Engine [In-process method call]
- Query Builder & Faceting Engine -> Search Engine Index [REST over mTLS]
- Core Services API -> Database [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- OpenSearch: Executes inverted-index queries for high-performance search (<800ms SLA).
- PostgreSQL with Debezium CDC: Streams real-time updates via replication protocol for strong consistency.
- Java & Spring Boot: Powers stateless API handlers, workers, and query engines.
- Kubernetes: Enables independent auto-scaling of services and data nodes.
- TLS 1.3 and mTLS: Secures all internal and external communication channels.

## Rationale
Decoupling the search layer using CDC and independent Java microservices prevents database bottlenecks and guarantees the sub-800ms search SLA. Restricting all components and data storage to EU infrastructure strictly satisfies regional compliance constraints.

- Web Portal [container] (React/TypeScript on Nginx)
- API Gateway [container] (Envoy/Kong)
- Core Services API [container] (Java/Spring Boot)
- Search & Catalogue Service [container] (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch)
- Database [container] (PostgreSQL with EU hosting)
- Identity Provider / SSO [externalSystem]
- Notification Gateway [externalSystem]
- Observability & Logging Platform [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Library Patrons / Circulation Staff -> Web Portal: HTTPS / TLS 1.3
- Web Portal -> API Gateway: HTTPS / JSON over TLS 1.3
- API Gateway -> Core Services API: gRPC over mTLS
- API Gateway -> Search & Catalogue Service: gRPC over mTLS
- Core Services API -> Database: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3 via PgBouncer
- Search & Catalogue Service -> Database: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3 via PgBouncer
- Core Services API -> Notification Gateway: Asynchronous HTTPS/REST webhooks over TLS 1.3

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript on Nginx: Delivers responsive self-service and administrative UIs
- Envoy/Kong: Provides robust API routing, edge security, and circuit breaking
- Java/Spring Boot: Implements scalable core business logic and transactional workflows
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch: Delivers sub-800ms high-performance catalogue search queries
- PostgreSQL with EU hosting: Ensures ACID compliance, row/column encryption, and EU data residency

## Rationale
- The chosen technology stack guarantees sub-800ms search performance while strictly adhering to EU data residency and GDPR mandates.
- Containerized microservices ensure high availability and scalability for both self-service patrons and administrative staff workflows.
